question.problem:
A rectangular plate of mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,3\le x\le 5,\,\,0\le y\le 1\}.$
Find the moment of inertia of this plate about the line $y=2.$
question.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, the distance between a point on $D$ and the line $y=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|y-2|.
$$

Next, the area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $A=2\cdot 1=2.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{M}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $y=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{5}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{M}{2}|y-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{5}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{M}{2}(y-2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{M}{2}({\int }_{3}^{5}\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{0}^{1}(y-2)^{2}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =\frac{M}{2}\cdot [x]_{3}^{5}\cdot {[\frac{1}{3}(y-2)^{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{M}{2}(5-3)(\frac{1}{3}(1-2)^{3}-\frac{1}{3}(0-2)^{3}) \\  & =M(-\frac{1}{3}+\frac{8}{3}) \\  & =\frac{7M}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
